text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ ALERT — increase in 502/504s and TCP reset counts for eu-west-2 /az-c private subnets. Service: hosted-api (/v1/embeddings). Error rate 12% over last 5m. Paging on-call @sam.

maya: saw the alert, jumping in. I just merged a tf change ~16:08 that moved a group of private subnets to a shared route table for egress optimization. Not sure if that touched az-c subnets.

sam: I'm on it. pulling up metrics & route tables. Can everyone hold changes until we triage? :hand:

liam: FYI customers in EU region reporting intermittent failures. Support just posted a handful of error traces (502 gateway) and connection resets.

support-bot: 5 customer tickets linked: #4721 #4723 #4729. Noted spike starting 16:05 UTC.

sam: checking VPC console... showing private-subnet-azc (subnet-0a1b2c3d) currently associated to rtb-shared-egress (rtb-0ddaa11). That RT has a 0.0.0.0/0 to nat-0fdeadbeef which is provisioned in az-b, not az-c. Looks like cross-az NAT target. That would explain asymmetric return path + resets.

alex: can you `describe-route-tables` snippet?

sam: paste: ```
$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rtb-0ddaa11 --region eu-west-2 
{
  "RouteTables": [
    {
      "RouteTableId": "rtb-0ddaa11",
      "Routes": [
        { "DestinationCidrBlock": "10.0.0.0/16", "GatewayId": null, "State": "active" },
        { "DestinationCidrBlock": "0.0.0.0/0", "NatGatewayId": "nat-0fdeadbeef", "State": "active" }
      ],
      "Associations": [ { "SubnetId": "subnet-0a1b2c3d", "Main": false } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

liam: nat-0fdeadbeef is in az-b and currently shows high retransmits on ASG metrics. Not healthy. If az-c instances' outbound hits az-b NAT then return path may get dropped or throttled.

maya: that matches — my tf change attempted to collapse per-az RT to a shared one to save a few minutes of config drift. I mistakenly fed module var `route_table_id = module.shared.rt` without pinning az-scoped RTs. My bad.

ops-bot: Deploy lock applied to repo infra/terraform/main at commit 0f4e2c. No further TF applies allowed during incident.

sam: mitigation options: 1) re-associate az-c private subnets back to their original per-az route table (rtb-0aabb22) — quickest. 2) create a new NAT gateway in az-c and update RT (longer). 3) force SNAT on the instances (not feasible). I'd prefer option 1 as immediate rollback.

jordan: i'll coordinate the rollback with network perms. @liam can you confirm rtb-0aabb22 exists and is the previous RT with NAT in az-c?

liam: confirmed. ```
$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=route-table-id,Values=rtb-0aabb22 --region eu-west-2
{
  "RouteTables": [ { "RouteTableId": "rtb-0aabb22", "Routes": [ { "DestinationCidrBlock": "0.0.0.0/0", "NatGatewayId": "nat-0cafe1234" } ] } ] }
```

nat-0cafe1234 is healthy and in az-c.

sam: ok +1 to re-associate. jordan, do the re-assoc and post the `associate-route-table` output. Keep changes to minimal scope: only subnet-0a1b2c3d and related private subnets in az-c.

maya: i'm ready to revert my tf module PR once we confirm services recover.

jordan: performing re-assoc now. running: ```
aws ec2 associate-route-table --subnet-id subnet-0a1b2c3d --route-table-id rtb-0aabb22 --region eu-west-2
```

jordan: assoc returned AssociationId: rtbassoc-07cb.

ops-bot: infrastructure change event logged: infra/terraform/main@0f4e2c -> manual-assoc by jordan.

sam: rolling metrics... error rate dropping from 12% -> 4% in last 90s. latency stabilizing. keep watch for 10m.

support-bot: customer ticket updates queued. Drafting message: "We've applied an emergency routing rollback in eu-west-2 AZ-c to restore connectivity. Monitoring for full recovery."

liam: doing quick health checks from a private instance in az-c: curl to embeddings endpoint now returns 200. TTLs look normal.

alex: can we snapshot the broken RT's associations to audit? Want to know if any other subnets were accidentally associated.

sam: good point. pulling all associations for rtb-0ddaa11: ```
$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rtb-0ddaa11 --region eu-west-2 
Associations: subnet-0a1b2c3d, subnet-0a1b2c9e (az-c), subnet-0b2c3d4e (az-b)
```
so az-b subnets also were on the shared table, which is fine. The regression came from az-c losing its az-local NAT path.

maya: i'll open an urgent PR to revert the shared-rt change and add a test that verifies each private subnet has a same-az NAT route.

sre-lead: +1 on revert and add gating smoke test on infra pipeline. Also schedule a postmortem with RCA and timeline in #postmortems.

sam: handing off to @jordan for on-call for next 2 hours. I'll stay in thread as backup. jordan, please escalate if anything else pops.

jordan: taking oncall. I'll monitor steady-state for 30m and coordinate with maya for the revert.

ops-bot: oncall-handoff: from sam -> jordan @ 16:18 UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigation in place, partial recovery observed. Impact: ~12% peak error rate during ~16:05-16:17 UTC. Current error rate 1.2%. Customers: 5 impacted (embedding-heavy customers). Priority: Sev 2.

support-bot: updated customer tickets with status and expected follow-ups.

maya: note for postmortem: root cause — Terraform module incorrectly allowed a single shared RT across AZs; missed invariant: per-az NAT topology. Contributing: lack of infra smoke test & missing infra PR reviewer with network context.

liam: follow-ups: 1) add infra unit test verifying `0.0.0.0/0` route points to nat in same AZ for private subnets, 2) add alert to detect cross-az nat hops > threshold, 3) run a tabletop on infra changes.

sre-lead: will assign action owners and schedule 72h follow-up.

jordan: logging the rollback change into incident timeline. Closing pager for oncall rotation in 30m if stable.

sam: thanks team. Great quick mitigation. Please file postmortem with timeline, diffs, and customer comms. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED -> monitoring-only at 16:47 UTC.

jordan: leaving final note here: confirmed 60m stable; will prepare runbook entry for "route table association rollback" and share with infra team tomorrow.

sre-lead: awarding +1 incident response kudos to the on-call and infra team.

support-bot: will follow up with affected customers with a root-cause summary once postmortem is published.

maya: opening PR to revert: infra/terraform/main#452-revert-shared-rt and adding smoke tests.

alex: thumbs up. we'll also add pre-merge CI check: `verify-az-nat-consistency`.

jordan: signing off on incident channel for now.
